solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Leak of crude oil messed with skin of seals

indicators.note: the letters of crude oil, plus the added pair, are messed about into a new order
the skin of a word is its outside, here the first and last letters of seals

explanation.surface: An oil spill has fouled the coats of the local seal colony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skin of' takes S and S, the outside letters of 'seals', and 'messed with' tells you to rearrange them with CRUDE OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A leak of information is a revelation of something kept secret.

clue.text: Piece of well-made, modern music from an unsigned band

indicators.note: Piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A polished, contemporary track is played by a band with no record deal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough recording sent to labels by bands seeking a contract is a sample tape.

clue.text: Drying agent — all but illegal — is manufactured without copyright

indicators.note: without means outside, so the rearranged letters sit around the copyright symbol
manufactured says the letters are made up into a new form
all but means every letter of illegal except the last

parts.note: C is the symbol and abbreviation for copyright

explanation.surface: A desiccant is made, nearly illegally, without permission from the rights holder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' trims ILLEGAL to ILLEGA; with IS, 'manufactured' rearranges them to SILIAGEL, and 'without' places that outside C.
explanation.definitionFit: The granules packed in sachets with new goods absorb moisture, a desiccant.

clue.text: Large, independent charity possibly making very specific terms

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an NGO, a non-governmental organisation, may be a charity

explanation.surface: A big independent charity is said to use very particular language.
explanation.definitionFit: Jargon peculiar to one trade or group is its special vocabulary.

clue.text: Rigorous thing boxers do — train regularly!

parts.note: boxers spar when practising

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of train, the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: A trainer urges boxers to keep up strict, regular training.
explanation.definitionFit: A harsh, austere regime with no comforts is severe and disciplined.

clue.text: Upstanding president takes time to withdraw

indicators.note: in a down clue, upstanding means the name stands upwards, read bottom to top

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was the 39th US president

explanation.surface: An upright president takes his time before backing down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upstanding' sounds like a compliment but turns CARTER into RETRAC.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a statement is to recant or pull it back.

clue.text: The high point is when one gets married

indicators.note: one word gets, or takes in, the other, so the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A wedding day is the peak of a person's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is not the person but ACE, the card counting as one, and 'gets' puts M (married) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The summit or peak of achievement is its pinnacle.

clue.text: Punch a friend

parts.note: to chin someone is to punch them on the jaw

explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so a china is a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyming-slang term means a pal or mate.

clue.text: Worker made matching boxes for fair

indicators.note: boxes means encloses, so the matching word holds the worker inside

parts.note: to even things is to make them match or balance
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A labourer makes matching crates for a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like a funfair but is the adjective meaning just; 'boxes' says the worker is enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating both sides equally is being impartial and just.

clue.text: Honey, in addition to fruit

parts.note: mel is Latin for honey, a term used in pharmacy
on can mean on top of or besides, as in 'on top of that'

explanation.surface: Someone is offered honey as well as some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: MEL is the Latin word for honey, still seen in old pharmacy terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantaloupe or watermelon is a kind of fruit.

clue.text: Watching musical, laid back, drinking wine

indicators.note: drinking means swallowing, so one piece takes the other inside it
laid back means set in reverse, so the show's name runs backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical about Eva Peron
tent is a deep red Spanish wine once used for communion

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes at a show with a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid back' turns the musical round to ATIVE, and 'drinking' takes the wine inside it. Tent is a Spanish red wine little known outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone paying close attention is observing carefully.

clue.text: Simple food, mostly with fresh tea

indicators.note: mostly means most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: nosh is slang for food

indicators.note: fresh says the letters of tea are made anew in a different order

explanation.surface: A basic meal is mostly eaten with freshly brewed tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims NOSH to NOS; 'fresh' rearranges TEA into EAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means easily done, no trouble at all.

clue.text: Actor hit Italy, then a country near there

indicators.note: hit suggests the letters of actor are knocked about into a new order

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An actor makes a hit in Italy and then goes to a neighbouring country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hit' looks like a stage success but signals rearranging ACTOR into CROAT; 'there' points back to Italy, just across the Adriatic.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balkan state lies across the Adriatic Sea from the Italian coast.

clue.text: Guitarist in AC/DC?

definitions.meaning: the stage name of the top-hatted Guns N' Roses lead guitarist
the oblique stroke printed between AC and DC is this punctuation mark

explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC is a rock band, so the clue seems to ask for one of its guitarists; in fact the guitarist belongs to Guns N' Roses, and the other sense is the stroke inside 'AC/DC'.
explanation.definitionFit: The forward stroke punctuation mark, and a famous rock guitarist's stage name.

clue.text: Mongrel enraged at first sign of some big dogs

indicators.note: mongrel means mixed, so the letters are mixed into a new order
the first sign of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: An angry mongrel attacks at the first sight of some large dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mongrel' looks like a dog in the picture but is the anagram signal for ENRAGED AT.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed is one of the tallest kinds of canine.

clue.text: Trendy resort that's in England, not Belgium!

indicators.note: not says the letter for Belgium is left out of the resort's name

parts.note: Brighton is a seaside resort on England's south coast
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A fashionable resort is praised as being in England rather than Belgium.
explanation.walkthrough: BRIGHTON is a lively seaside town south of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Being right-on means holding fashionable, progressive views, so the phrase fits up-to-date and modish.

clue.text: Tax rises are about to overwhelm new European restaurant

indicators.note: in a down clue, rises means the word reads upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: VAT, value added tax, is the UK sales tax

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the turned word takes the other letter inside
about means turned round, so the little word is read backwards

explanation.surface: Rising taxes are about to swamp a new eatery in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rises' and 'about' each signal a turnaround; 'about' gives ERA, and 'to overwhelm' puts N inside it. VAT is the UK's sales tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek eating house, a small tavern serving food, is the sense.

clue.text: Tense debate in anti-government action

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
to reason is to argue or debate a matter

explanation.surface: A tense debate takes place over a protest against the government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' reads as an adjective for the debate but is just T.
explanation.definitionFit: Betraying one's country or plotting to overthrow its rulers is the crime meant.

clue.text: Principal lawsuit covering the start of ill-fated flight

indicators.note: covering means one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: the star is the principal performer

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit in court

explanation.surface: A senior lawsuit hangs over the beginning of a doomed flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' suggests an air journey but means a set of steps; STAR covers I.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a set of steps between floors.

clue.text: Very mindful of extremely atypical partner

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extremes, the first and last letters, of atypical

parts.note: a lover is a romantic partner

explanation.surface: Someone is deeply aware of an unusual partner.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all over someone is to lavish attention on them, being keenly attentive.

clue.text: Dead body is still

definitions.meaning: a corpse, the mortal leftovers of a person

explanation.surface: A corpse lies motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: A corpse is mortal leftovers, and staying is continuing.

clue.text: Old, empty toilet in prison house

indicators.note: in says the first pieces are placed inside the word for prison

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison

indicators.note: empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving just the outer two of toilet

explanation.surface: An old, unused lavatory sits in a jail building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' strips 'toilet' to its outer two letters; 'in' then places those and the O inside the prison word.
explanation.definitionFit: A small country dwelling is a type of home.

clue.text: Put something in the base of solar battery unit

parts.note: to charge is to load or fill, as one charges a glass

indicators.note: in a down clue the base of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone fits a component at the bottom of a solar battery unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that replenishes batteries, sometimes powered by solar panels.

clue.text: Doctor carries performance enhancer around for cheating athlete

indicators.note: the doctor's letters carry, or hold, the other piece inside
around means the drug's letters are turned round

parts.note: EPO, erythropoietin, is a banned blood-boosting drug in sport

explanation.surface: A team doctor carries a banned drug to help a cheating athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns the drug's letters to OPE, and 'carries' holds them inside. EPO is a blood-boosting drug notorious in cycling.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone taking banned drugs to compete is a drug cheat.

clue.text: Endangered animal in the outer parts of Patagonia?

indicators.note: the outer parts of a place name are its first and last letters, which the solver must name aloud with a joining word

parts.note: the region at the southern tip of South America, here only a source of its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An endangered creature might live in the far reaches of Patagonia.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the animal does not live there: the outer letters of 'Patagonia' are P AND A, which run together gives the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The black-and-white bear of China is a symbol of threatened species.

clue.text: Many changes spoil part of South-east Asia

indicators.note: changes says the letters of many are altered into a new order

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage

explanation.surface: Too many alterations ruin a region of South-east Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges MANY to MYAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The country formerly called Burma lies in the south-east of the continent.

clue.text: I'm upset and assume a potentially silly position

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the letters read upwards

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on, to assume them

explanation.surface: Someone upset adopts a pose that may look foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, mid-on is a fielding position; moved close to the bat it becomes 'silly mid-on', so the position is 'potentially silly'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cricket fielding spot can be brought in close, when it is called silly.

clue.text: Rider on way over here

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a rider is an addition to a document, like a postscript, PS
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A rider on the road is called over.
explanation.definitionFit: The whispered interjection is used to catch someone's attention discreetly.

clue.text: Being on the bench/left out is unrewarding

indicators.note: out says the letter for left is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: a substitute on the bench is non-playing

explanation.surface: Sitting on the bench, dropped from the side, brings no reward.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash just separates two pieces; 'left out' removes L.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-paying task brings in no money, so it is unremunerative.

clue.text: US narcos oddly lose supplies of drugs

parts.note: the DEA, the Drug Enforcement Administration, employs America's narcotics agents

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of lose, the first and third

explanation.surface: American drug agents oddly fail to stop narcotics shipments.
explanation.walkthrough: The DEA is the US federal drug agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Drug transactions, such as a dealer's sales, are what the plural means.

clue.text: Small, pale-coloured bird

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
wan means pale and sickly-looking

explanation.surface: A little, pale bird is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The long-necked white waterfowl is a large bird.

clue.text: Styptic thread in a hospital department

indicators.note: in says the thread goes inside the other letters

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
string is a length of thread or cord

explanation.surface: A styptic dressing thread is found in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Styptic' is a medical word for something that stops bleeding by contracting tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: A styptic draws tissues together to stem bleeding, as an astringent lotion does.
